title: I'm Building My Own 2.5D Platformer in Unreal Engine 5 — I'd Love Your Feedback!
author: Sashamirae17
selftext:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm an indie developer currently working on **Bollum**, a 2.5D physics-based platformer that I'm building from the ground up using Unreal Engine 5.

The game is still in its early stages, but I have a lot of ideas that I want to bring to life!

🎮 **What's the idea behind Bollum?**

I'm working on creating a fun and challenging platformer where movement, momentum, gravity, bouncing, and physics play a big role in the gameplay.

My goal is to build something that starts with simple mechanics but gradually evolves into a much bigger and more interesting experience, with unique environments, creative obstacles, challenging levels, and potentially even competitive multiplayer modes.

🛠️ **Where am I right now?**

At the moment, I'm focusing on building a solid foundation for the game.

That includes working on movement mechanics, gravity, collision physics, wall bouncing, slope interactions, and all the little details that make gameplay feel satisfying.

And yes... I've already encountered quite a few bugs along the way! 😅

🚀 **Why am I sharing this?**

I've started a YouTube channel called **Vornum Studios**, where I'm documenting the development process through devlogs.

I want to share not only the successful moments but also the problems, experiments, mistakes, and solutions that come with developing a game.

But more importantly, **I'd love to involve the community in this journey.**

I'm genuinely interested in hearing your ideas, suggestions, and constructive criticism.

What mechanics would you love to see in a physics-based platformer? What would make a game like this really fun or unique?

Even small suggestions could help shape the future of Bollum!

❤️ **Want to support the project?**

If you like the idea and want to follow the development, I'd really appreciate it if you checked out my YouTube channel and subscribed.

It would mean a lot to have people following the journey, sharing feedback, and helping me make Bollum the best game I can possibly create.

🎥 **YouTube — Vornum Studios**

[https://www.youtube.com/@VornumStudios](https://www.youtube.com/@VornumStudios)

This is just the beginning, and there's still a long way to go.

Thanks for taking the time to read this, and I'd love to hear what you think! ❤️

— Vornum Studios
